memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "For six years you are to sow your fields and harvest the crops, but during the seventh year let the land lie unplowed and unused. Then the poor among your people may get food from it, and the wild animals may eat what is left. Do the same with your vineyard and your olive grove." - Exodus 23:10-11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God builds rest and generosity right into the rhythm of the land. Six years of work, then a year in which the fields lie fallow. And notice the beautiful purpose: whatever grows on its own that year is left for the poor and even for the wild animals. God ties rest and care for the needy together, teaching His people to trust Him rather than to grasp and hoard without end.

This required real faith. To let a field rest for a whole year meant trusting that God would provide enough in the other years to carry them through. It was a yearly lesson that their security did not come from ceaseless labour but from the God who feeds His people. The land's rest preached a sermon: you can stop striving, because the Lord provides.

We need this lesson deeply. Our world runs on relentless productivity, and we can easily believe that our worth and safety depend on how much we produce. But God invites us into rhythms of rest that declare our trust in Him. And He weaves generosity into that rest — the fallow field fed the poor. When we loosen our grip on constant getting, we find we have more room to give. May God teach us to rest in His provision and to open our hands to those in need.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I trust God enough to build genuine rest into my life?
How might loosening my grip on constant productivity free me to be more generous?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You are my provider, not my endless striving. Teach me to rest in Your provision and to open my hands generously to those in need. Amen.
